chunks: 33. My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mus'adah ibn Sadaqah, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both),
that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah has cursed those who made their religion a means of greed/striving, meaning argumentation, to refute the truth with falsehood.'

key_terms.شُحًّا: Greed or striving (for victory in debate)
key_terms.لِيَدْفَعُوا الْحَقَّ بِالْبَاطِلِ: To refute the truth with falsehood

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to make religion a means of 'shuh' (greed/striving) in argument?
ai.summary: In al-Tawhid, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to illustrate the corruption of religious discourse when debate becomes an end in itself, prioritizing rhetorical victory over divine truth. This curse specifically targets those who weaponize 'shuh' (greed or ambition) to distort reality, a key theme in Shia epistemology regarding the purity of intention in theological discussion. It serves as a warning against intellectual arrogance that leads to the suppression of Haqq (truth) through Batil (falsehood).
